value.title: Uniform receiver-curve continuum bridge and 30-row stability
value.summary:
Accepted statement:

Using the accepted premise-bound 30-row system and finite-grid posterior-measure reduction of transactions e3c1036ca607539a5ebcddf3058e6014ac5c1cd9 and e2bbc1e210e496b3c834e658820fc90287f3b2c0, respectively: (i) every binary-input receiver curve obeys |J_A(p)-J_A(p')| <= 2 h_2(|p-p'|); (ii) the generalized mean-one-half posterior-measure receiver curves form a compact subset of C([0,1]) whose finite-output curves are uniformly dense, and for every N-point grid Q containing {0,1/2,1} there is an at-most-N-output exact grid match with sup-norm error at most min{1,4 h_2(Delta_Q)}, preserving an already reflected pair on reflection-closed Q; and (iii) replacing G,K by curves within epsilon_G,epsilon_K changes every one of the accepted 30 row right sides by at most a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K with the displayed audited coefficients, universally at most 4 epsilon_G+4 epsilon_K. Hence the same hierarchy is feasible under those explicit row relaxations, and strictly feasible witnesses persist under sufficiently fine approximations. No unrelaxed optimized-value convergence, exact full-functional cardinality, reflected optimality, minimax interchange, numerical capacity improvement, or exact sum-capacity is asserted.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- Validity is premise-bound to the accepted 30-row system from e3c1036ca607539a5ebcddf3058e6014ac5c1cd9, including its external theorem premise.
- The approximation result preserves an already reflected receiver pair on a reflection-closed grid; it does not symmetrize arbitrary pairs or establish reflected optimality.
- Feasibility is established under explicit row relaxations; no unrelaxed optimized-value convergence is proved.
- No exact full-functional cardinality bound, minimax interchange, numerical capacity improvement, or exact sum-capacity is established.
- Computational attestations check the encoded dependency list, 30-row coefficient algebra, global coefficient bound, and tested grid formulas; the entropy, compactness, Carathéodory, and arbitrary-grid arguments are established mathematically rather than by those computations.

value.title: Receiver-curve continuity, compactness, approximation, and stability proof
value.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It uses a common-mixture entropy argument for the alphabet-independent binary-input modulus; the mean-one-half posterior-measure representation, weak compactness, and the common modulus for compactness in the uniform norm; Carathéodory exact matching on finite grids followed by the modulus for the stated full-curve error; and posterior-conditioning identities together with the accepted receiver-term audit to bound perturbations of all 30 row right sides. The final step transfers feasible hierarchies to explicitly row-relaxed systems and preserves witnesses having sufficient strict slack. This proof item is limited to the linked claim and does not establish any excluded unrelaxed convergence, cardinality, reflected-optimality, minimax, numerical-capacity, or exact-capacity conclusion.

value.title: Deterministic 30-row receiver-curve stability audit
value.summary: Tool used for the computationally audited portion of the linked accepted claim. It checks the exact required-dependency list, independently rebuilds the accepted generic 30-row path system, combines identical signed receiver terms, verifies every displayed rowwise stability-coefficient pair and the universal (4,4) coefficient bound, and checks the tested reflected uniform-grid support and mesh formulas. It does not computationally prove the entropy-continuity, compactness, Carathéodory, or arbitrary-grid arguments.

placementAudits.rationale: The accepted claim directly advances the existing auxiliary-receiver converse objective by connecting its finite-grid posterior representation to compact uniform receiver curves and by quantifying stability of the accepted 30-row system. Its scope does not directly span the incomparable code-induced-converse or relaxed-UV-functional programs.
